name: Greater German Reich

areaKm2.note: world_1938 Germany polygon (incl. Austria and Sudetenland) = ~560,000 km2 computed on the sphere (low); plus annexed Polish territories (~92,000), Danzig, Memel and de facto Alsace-Lorraine and Luxembourg = ~700,000 km2 (mid). Protectorate (48,900) in the high bound.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1944 = 90,238k (Greater German Reich incl. Austria, Sudetenland and annexed Polish and western territories, mid); Harrison 1998 Table 1-1: Germany 68.6M + Austria 6.8M in 1938 (low ~80M after Sudetenland). Protectorate of Bohemia-Moravia and General Government excluded.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share Germany 1940 = 53.2% (mid). Low = COW upop/tpop 1944 = 25,412/90,238 = 0.28 (cities over 100,000); evacuation of bombed cities lowered the 1944 figure.

activePersonnel.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-5: German armed forces 9,420,000 in 1944 (Heer, Waffen-SS, Luftwaffe, Kriegsmarine). Snapshot: June 1944. Check: COW NMC v7 milper 1944 = 6,128k (annual averages, not the snapshot-date strength).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Almost every trained man was already in uniform; reserves = convalescents and the untrained Volkssturm (from October 1944).

supportPersonnel.note: Cited page: Luftwaffe ~3M (Nov 1943-Jun 1944) incl. 1.7M male soldiers, anti-aircraft units 600,000 soldiers; plus Kriegsmarine (~0.8M), Replacement Army (~2.5M) and the field army's artillery, panzer, engineer and service troops. Derived as active minus infantry and cavalry.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Ellis, World War II: The Statistical Survey (isbn:0-8160-2971-7), not read from a fetched source. ~17.9M men served in the Wehrmacht 1939-45 (Ellis, Statistical Survey) / ~90M = 0.2.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Zaloga, Bagration 1944 (isbn:1-85532-478-4), not read from a fetched source. ~250 infantry, Volksgrenadier and SS divisions at 2,000-6,000 riflemen each by mid-1944. Bagration infobox: Army Group Centre 486,493 combat personnel of ~849,000 total.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: MG 42, StG 44 (from 1944), Panzerfaust and Panzerschreck

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: veteran cadres, shortened training for new drafts

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Zaloga, Bagration 1944 (isbn:1-85532-478-4), not read from a fetched source. Mountain (Gebirgs), Jaeger and Fallschirmjaeger divisions.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: same weapons, mountain equipment

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: elite units

count.note: Educated guess. Cavalry brigades and SS cavalry divisions (Florian Geyer) on the Eastern Front.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: no specific evidence beyond the era-typical row

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: anti-partisan duty

count.note: Educated guess. Tanks, assault guns and tank destroyers in June 1944 (Pz IV, Panther, Tiger, StuG III/IV, Jagdpanzer); Bagration infobox: 118 tanks and 452 assault guns in Army Group Centre.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 1.0 (best of era). Evidence: Panther and Tiger outclassed Allied tanks; StuG the most numerous

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: experienced crews, fuel short for training

count.note: Educated guess. Field and heavy guns and howitzers (excl. AT, AA and mortars); Bagration infobox (Soviet sources): 7,760 field guns in Army Group Centre.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: leFH 18, sFH 18, Nebelwerfer

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: flexible fire direction, ammunition short

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Ellis, World War II: The Statistical Survey (isbn:0-8160-2971-7), not read from a fetched source. Single- and twin-engine day and night fighters in June 1944 (Ellis, Statistical Survey); most in Reich air defence.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Bf 109G, Fw 190A; Me 262 not yet operational

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: pilot crisis: new pilots with ~110 hours, veterans lost over the Reich

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Ellis, World War II: The Statistical Survey (isbn:0-8160-2971-7), not read from a fetched source. Bombers, ground-attack and reconnaissance aircraft in June 1944; Bagration infobox: 920 aircraft with Luftflotte 6.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Ju 88, He 177, Fw 190F/G, Ju 87G

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: fuel shortage

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1922-1946 (isbn:0-85177-146-7), not read from a fetched source. Battleships, cruisers and destroyers. Tirpitz, Luetzow, Admiral Scheer, Prinz Eugen, Admiral Hipper, Nuernberg, Leipzig, Emden, Koeln; old battleships Schlesien and Schleswig-Holstein (high) = 9/11/11. Scharnhorst sunk December 1943. Plus ~15-20 destroyers in commission in mid-1944 = 15/15/20 (mid at 15 so the minor mid keeps the ~20 fleet torpedo boats). Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor.

quality.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.75/0.8/0.85 (11) and destroyers 0.7/0.75/0.8 (15), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: quality 0.75-1.0 and 0.75. Evidence: Tirpitz the most powerful ship in European waters; large destroyers with 15 cm guns

training.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.6/0.65/0.7 (11) and destroyers 0.65/0.7/0.75 (15), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: little sea time

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1922-1946 (isbn:0-85177-146-7), not read from a fetched source. ~20 fleet torpedo boats in commission in mid-1944. The ~15-20 destroyers moved to ships_major (was 25/35/45), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: large destroyers with 15 cm guns

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: no specific evidence beyond the era-typical row

count.note: Educated guess. U-boats in commission in June 1944 (~430 incl. training boats, mid); ~160-190 front boats (low).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Type VIIC with schnorkel; Type XXI not yet operational

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Kriegsmarine page: 28,000 of 40,000 U-boat crewmen killed in the war

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Westermann, Flak (isbn:0-7006-1136-3), not read from a fetched source. Flak batteries in mid-1944, ~2,600 heavy (8.8-12.8 cm) and ~1,600 light (Westermann, Flak). Luftwaffe page: 600,000 soldiers and 530,000 auxiliaries in the anti-aircraft units in Oct 1944. Bagration infobox (Soviet sources): 2,320 AA guns with Army Group Centre.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 1.0. Evidence: 8.8 and 12.8 cm guns, Wuerzburg radar fire control

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: many crews were Luftwaffenhelfer schoolboys and auxiliaries

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: excellent tactical and operational commanders hamstrung by Hitler's no-retreat orders (Bagration, Normandy)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: units fought on after catastrophic losses; Kampfgruppen; 20 July plot

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5. Evidence: two-front war being lost; ideological units fanatical

weapons.note: Anchor: 8 (1943). Evidence: MG 42, StG 44, Panzerfaust, 8.8 cm Pak 43, V-1 (from 13 June 1944)

armor.note: Anchor: 8 (1943, rolled homogeneous armour). Evidence: Panther, Tiger I, King Tiger entering service

ships.note: Anchor: 8 (1943). Evidence: Type XXI electro-boat building, schnorkel; surface fleet small

fortification.note: Anchor: 8 (1943). Evidence: Atlantic Wall, U-boat pens, flak towers

logistics.note: Anchor: between 7 (railways) and 8. Evidence: rail-dependent, ~1.2M horses with the army, fuel crisis after May 1944

communications.note: Anchor: 8 (1943). Evidence: radio nets, Enigma (read by the Allies)

isr.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: air reconnaissance lost over the West; radar network

air.note: Anchor: 8 (1943). Evidence: Me 262 jet and Me 163 rocket fighter entering service mid-1944, V-1

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): Germany 1944 = 9,698, Austria 1944 = 6,618 (2011 int$); annexed eastern territories poorer; Greater Reich ~9,400.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-8: German military burden 70% of national income in 1943 (23% in 1939); 1944 similar.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry incl. war production ~50% of output.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment. Cited page: in 1937, 29% of the employed in Germany (9,388,000 people) worked in agriculture. 1 - 0.29 = 0.71 (mid); low allows for the more agrarian annexed eastern territories; by early 1945 foreigners were a third of the agricultural labour force (cited page). Germany fed itself partly by extraction from occupied Europe.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching 18 per year in the Greater Reich (births ~1.3M c. 1926).

armor.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: tanks and SPGs 18,300 in 1944 (Germany).

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Total combat aircraft read from Harrison 1998 Table 1-6; fighter share recalled, not read from a fetched source. Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: 34,100 combat aircraft in 1944 (Luftwaffe page: ~36,000); ~25,000 were fighters under the Jaegernotprogramm (split).

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Total combat aircraft read from Harrison 1998 Table 1-6; fighter share recalled, not read from a fetched source. Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: 34,100 combat aircraft in 1944 less ~25,000 fighters.

artillery.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: 148,000 guns in 1944 (all calibres incl. AT and AA, as in the ussr-1941 snapshot); field artillery alone ~40,000-70,000 (low).

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Destroyers and fleet torpedo boats per year 1943-44.

air_defense.note: Educated guess. Flak batteries' worth of guns per year (8.8 cm ~5,000+ per year in 1944, plus light guns).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Roads of the Greater Reich incl. ~3,800 km of Autobahn.

railKm.note: Educated guess. CHAT railline Germany 1940 = 61,940 km (read from https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, low); lines in the annexed Polish and western territories guessed.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1922-1946 (isbn:0-85177-146-7), not read from a fetched source. Hamburg, Bremen, Kiel, Wilhelmshaven, Stettin, Koenigsberg, Gotenhafen, Danzig.

merchantTonnage.note: League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40 table: German merchant fleet 4,244,000 GRT (June 1938, high); by 1944 ~1/3 lost, trapped abroad or seized (mid ~2.5M GRT, educated guess). Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Rail and horse-drawn supply in the East; Allied air attack crippled French railways before Normandy.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses in the Reich (~3.5M) of which ~1.2M with the army.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: fortified cities and rivers, population support; no climate depth.

notes: Snapshot date June 1944 (Normandy landings 6 June; Operation Bagration 22 June). Territory = the Greater German Reich (Germany, Austria, Sudetenland, annexed Polish and western territories); occupied Europe (France, the Low Countries, Norway, the General Government, the occupied USSR, Italy, Hungary from March 1944) not counted as territory; basesAbroad lists key positions. The border uses world_1938 (nearest at or before 1944). Forces are the whole Wehrmacht incl. Waffen-SS. Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries).
